title: A Tide for the Postcard
premise: Five years after a catastrophic final performance ended his concert career, cellist Emrys Coldharbour lives by small safe steps: teaching, repairing instruments, never playing in public. When his sister begs him to bring a date to the family reunion, he hires Wren, a ferry-schedule-obsessed postcard artist who owes him a favor — and the fake relationship turns real over dessert. But Wren is secretly writing a serialized comic about a disgraced musician that mirrors Emrys's collapse, and when the truth surfaces mid-reunion, his family's old wounds and Wren's ambition collide with his fragile recovery. In the climax, Emrys must choose between accepting a career-saving comeback offer and boarding the last ferry of the season to tell Wren the truth first; he chooses the ferry, plays publicly for the first time on its deck, and they begin something honest as the boat pulls away.
about_author: Emrys Eastwick is the pen name of a former orchestral librarian who spent a decade backstage before turning to fiction. They write love stories set in coastal towns where music, memory, and tide charts govern everything.

chapters.title: The Tuning Fork
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Five years after walking off stage mid-concerto, Emrys teaches cello to children and repairs instruments in the seaside town of Gullhaven. A request to play at a wedding sends him into a panic attack he hides from everyone. Beat: establish the safe, small life and its hidden cost.

chapters.title: Postcards from Wren
chapters.summary: Wren POV. Wren Ashcombe sells hand-painted postcards at the ferry dock and secretly draws a webcomic about 'the Cellist Who Vanished.' Emrys buys a postcard of the concert hall he once played; Wren recognizes him and says nothing. Beat: curiosity kindles, secrets planted.

chapters.title: A Favor Owed
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Emrys once fixed Wren's flooded studio rent-free; now Wren repays it. Emrys's sister Priya demands he bring a partner to the Coldharbour family reunion or face their mother's matchmaking. He asks Wren to be his fake date for one weekend. Beat: the deal struck, both hiding motives.

chapters.title: Rehearsing a Lie
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Over two days of 'practice dates,' Emrys and Wren build a believable backstory — how they met, first kiss, inside jokes — until the invented details start feeling like memories. Beat: intimacy disguised as rehearsal.

chapters.title: The Crossing
chapters.summary: Wren POV. The ferry ride to Harrow Isle for the reunion. Wren observes Emrys white-knuckled at the rail, learns his performance trauma involves more than stage fright. First real conversation beneath the act. Beat: empathy begins to breach the contract.

chapters.title: Coldharbour House
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Arrival at the family estate: critical mother Vivienne, golden-boy brother Julian, and Priya, who knows the truth of the final performance. Emrys performs 'happy couple' flawlessly while drowning. Beat: the past has architecture here.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the reunion dinner, under pressure from Vivienne's probing, the fake story holds — too well. A stolen moment in the pantry becomes an almost-real kiss. Both retreat confused. Beat: the line between act and truth dissolves by dessert.

chapters.title: The Comic
chapters.summary: Wren POV. Wren's editor reveals the 'Cellist Who Vanished' comic has gone viral — and readers are identifying the real musician. Wren faces a choice: reveal the source or protect Emrys. Meanwhile Emrys finds a sketchbook page of himself. Beat: secret tightens.

chapters.title: Julian's Offer
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Brother Julian, a festival director, offers Emrys a comeback slot — the career-saving opportunity everyone says he needs. Emrys can't say no without explaining everything. Wren encourages him, guiltily aware of the comic. Beat: hope arrives wearing pressure.

chapters.title: Tide Charts and Truths
chapters.summary: Wren POV. Wren and Emrys spend a day mapping tide pools; Wren nearly confesses the comic twice. Instead they share real histories — Wren's estranged father, Emrys's ruined hands and ruined reputation. Beat: genuine love takes root in borrowed time.

chapters.title: Priya Knows
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Priya confronts Emrys: she saw him kiss Wren like it wasn't acting, and warns him the family will devour anyone who gets close. She also hints she knows someone is writing about him. Beat: warning shot; stakes sharpen.

chapters.title: The Serialization
chapters.summary: Wren POV. The comic's latest installment depicts the catastrophic final performance in devastating detail — details only the cellist could know. Comments speculate wildly. Wren's editor wants the reveal issue for maximum impact. Beat: deadline versus loyalty.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A storm strands everyone on Harrow Island; the last ferry of the season looms in three days. Confined together, Emrys and Wren grow closer while the family fractures over old grievances about Emrys's fall. Beat: pressure cooker sealed.

chapters.title: What the Hands Remember
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Julian pushes Emrys to rehearse for the comeback; alone with a cello, Emrys discovers his hands still work — what broke was trust, not tendon. He almost tells Wren everything, but catches her sketching him. Beat: breakthrough shadowed by suspicion.

chapters.title: The Reveal Issue
chapters.summary: Wren POV. Cornered by her editor and the viral speculation, Wren publishes the reveal: the comic is drawn from life, and the Cellist is real. She plans to tell Emrys herself — but the issue posts early. Beat: the choice made for her.

chapters.title: Betrayal in B Flat
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. The family reads the comic aloud at breakfast like a verdict. Emrys realizes every intimate moment was also material. He confronts Wren before the whole house; she cannot deny it. He walks into the storm. Beat: heartbreak at full volume.

chapters.title: Vivienne's Ledger
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. His mother, unexpectedly gentle, finally tells him why the family weaponized his failure: fear, not cruelty. She admits the comeback offer is Julian's redemption arc, not Emrys's. Beat: the price of survival named at last.

chapters.title: Ink and Water
chapters.summary: Wren POV. Wren, devastated, reads her own comic honestly for the first time and sees she drew not exploitation but grief — hers, inherited from a father who abandoned art. She writes a final issue: an apology, and the truth of falling in love. Beat: accountability as devotion.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Comeback day arrives — and so does the last ferry. Emrys must choose the stage or the dock. He chooses the dock, boards the ferry to find Wren, and learns she stayed behind to find him. They miss each other by minutes. Beat: darkest hour before resolution.

chapters.title: Cello on the Deck
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. On the ferry's return crossing, Emrys does the unthinkable: plays publicly, unannounced, for strangers and gulls — the piece he fled five years ago. Passengers weep. Wren, chasing along the quay, hears it carry across the water. Beat: catharsis through music.

chapters.title: A Tide for the Postcard
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Wren meets the returning ferry; Emrys forgives her, having read her apology issue — she drew his survival, not his shame. He declines Julian's festival but proposes teaching a community orchestra with Wren illustrating the programs. Beat: loyalty and truth reconciled.

chapters.title: First Movement
chapters.summary: Epilogue, dual POV. Spring in Gullhaven: the community orchestra's first wobbly concert, Wren's new comic about beginnings rather than falls, a postcard on Emrys's wall of two figures on a ferry deck. Small steps, taken together. Beat: found family, earned love, quiet joy.
